subject: Egress gateway binding and safelist scoping for private endpoint deployment
messages:
From: security@acme-health.com

Cc: sre@novacorp.com
Date: Sat, 17 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify egress gateway binding / safelist scope for private runtime

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Our security team is documenting the final egress controls we require for the Redwood private runtime deployed inside our VPC. Two specific asks: (1) we need a tight list of IPs (or FQDNs) that the control plane and runtime will talk to from our subnet for audit/a dn firewall rules; (2) confirmation of whether traffic will exit via a customer-owned NAT gateway or a Redwood-managed egress gateway (and how that affects rotation/ephemeral addresses).

Can you provide: a recommended scoping model (per-runtime IPs vs. shared egress), port/FQDN requirements, TLS/SNI expectations, and any proxy mTLS expectations? We also need the list in CSV for our firewall team.

Thanks — please loop in ops if needed.

—Chris (Acme Health Security)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Chris <security@acme-health.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify egress gateway binding / safelist scope for private runtime

Hi Chris — thanks, and good questions. High-level summary up front: Redwood supports both models: (A) customer-managed NAT (recommended for strict ownership), and (B) Redwood-managed egress gateway (useful when customers want less ops overhead). The scoping implications differ, so I outlined both with concrete artefacts attached.

Quick answers:
- IP/FQDN: For customer-managed NAT, allowlist our control-plane FQDNs (control.redwood-inference.com) and the runtime model pull FQDNs (models.redwood-inference.com) and the ports below. For Redwood-managed egress, we provide a small set of static IPs per-tenant dedicated pool (CSV attached).
- Ports/TLS: Outbound to 443 (HTTPS) for model pulls, health checks, and telemetry. Additional ephemeral ports may be used for long-lived streaming (we surface ports but traffic remains TLS 1.2+/mTLS where requested).
- Proxy/mTLS: If you require mTLS for outbound to control plane, we can enable client cert auth for the control plane only; runtime to model artifact storage currently uses TLS with optional signed tokens.
- Rotation: For Redwood-managed egress we perform scheduled rotations; we publish rotation windows and new IPs 72 hours before change. For customer NAT, rotations are under your control.

Attachments: egress-ip-list.csv (tenant static IPs for Redwood-managed), private-runtime-egress-diagram.png, egress-sla-playbook.pdf.

Questions for your firewall team: do you allow FQDN-based rules (SNI-based allowlist) or require strict source IPs? If SNI allowed, we can simplify to FQDNs only. If not, the CSV includes per-tenant static IPs and suggested ephemeral ranges for streaming fallbacks.

I'll summarize decisions/actions below and tag owners.

Action items (initial):
- David: confirm behavior for long-lived streaming connections and provide exact ephemeral port ranges. (Owner: david_kim)
- Laura: draft rotation notice template and publish cadence for Reddit-managed egress IP rotation. (Owner: laura_bennett)
- Chris: confirm whether Acme will accept SNI-based allowlisting or wants source IPs only. (Owner: acme-sec)

If it's easier, we can stand up a 30-min call with your network team.

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

On Tue, Jun 19, 2028 at 10:03 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick answers:
> - IP/FQDN: For customer-managed NAT, allowlist our control-plane FQDNs ... For Redwood-managed egress, we provide a small set of static IPs per-tenant dedicated pool (CSV attached).

Chris — a couple of implementation details from runtime side:
- Streaming (LLM token stream): we maintain long-lived TLS connections over 443. The client originates the connection to our runtime endpoints; for streaming we re-use connections but do not require extra ephemeral source ports beyond standard TCP ephemeral range. We recommend allowing ephemeral source ranges 32768-60999 only if you plan to restrict by source port (most teams do not).
- Connection pinning: if deployed in VPC with a private endpoint, you can pin a subnet to our connector; that connector will perform outbound connections (either via your NAT or our egress). If you choose Redwood-managed egress, the outbound source IP will be one of the tenant static IPs in the CSV. If you choose customer NAT, source IPs will be your NAT's public IPs.
- Health checks and telemetry: 443 to metrics.redwood-inference.com and traces.redwood-inference.com. These endpoints accept TLS with token auth; no client cert required unless you opt-in for mTLS.
- FQDN SNI: we set the server_name to control.redwood-inference.com for control plane calls and models.redwood-inference.com for model pulls. If your firewall can do SNI inspection and allow control.redwood-inference.com, that is the least brittle model.

I'll attach a short port matrix in the next email.

—David
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

Thanks, team. Chris — following up on next steps so we can close this out for your audit: 

1) Decision needed from Acme: choose model A (customer NAT) or B (Redwood-managed egress). If you pick A, provide the public IP address(es) we'll expect inbound for control-plane callbacks (we will supply the FQDNs to allow inbound from). If you pick B, accept the attached CSV as the source IPs for your firewall.
2) If Acme accepts SNI-based allowlisting, we will prepare a minimal FQDN-only checklist for your firewall (control.redwood-inference.com, models.redwood-inference.com, metrics.redwood-inference.com).
3) David will send a short port matrix (ETA: 24 hours) and Laura will publish the rotation/cert notice doc (ETA: 48 hours).

I recommend a quick 20-minute joint call with your network ops to confirm the CSV format and any logging requirements (we can produce a short evidence pack for SOC review). Please let us know availability — we have slots tomorrow 11:00-13:00 PT or Friday 09:00-11:00 PT.
